Excessive bail shall not be required, nor excessive fines imposed, nor cruel and unusual punishments inflicted.

Bail is a means to make sure your ass appears before the judge for a serious crime, drunk in public is not exactly a serious crime. The whole judicial system needs to be reformed from the bottom up.

This only makes some sense if we're talking about misdemeanors, in my opinion. If someone rapes or murders, they shouldn't be released because they cannot afford bail. If someone is caught with a bit of weed and cannot afford bail, they should be let go, sure. But, then this brings up the whole question of "why have bail in the first place?" if the only people who are going to be effected by it are those with more money.

The idea that someone who is poor is treated more favorably than someone with money is ridiculous. If you're poor and you're awaiting trial, you get out without paying bail. I think it's a great idea to not have anyone pay bail for misdemeanors, and instead make them all do check-ins. More serious crimes, of course, shouldn't take away bail.

But, regardless, it does seem kind of overt that a suspected criminal can, in some ways, buy his or her freedom, even if they're being tried for murder or rape; they just need enough money to pay the bail (if there is one.)

Courts evaluate bail based on several factors such as, flight risk being the biggest one, but also the nature of the crime, the likelihood of the defendant re-offending before trial, the safety of the community etc. If you're wealthy, you likely have strong ties within the community, a life you've built mingled with people, community service, and business, which most people will not leave; they'd rather defend their way of life... that's the assumption anyway. I agree, though, it's not a fair system in its current form; however, pushes like these that try to facilitate change for the better means we're headed in the right direction.
